newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 16.

text.p: Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers union continued to negotiate a new contract late Sunday night, while 13,000 members of the Canadian Auto Workers union at Chrysler Corp threatened a strike for Wednesday unless certain demands are met, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
* Navistar International Corp said it will not make its next generation truck as a result of negotiations with the UAW.

* The Dow Jones industrial average rose Friday to close at a record level of 5838.52, while bond prices also rallied as Wall Street cheered economic data that showed a decreasing likelihood for the adoption of higher interest rates at the next meeting of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee on September 24.

* New York State Public Service Commission Chairman John O'Mara said he would vote against the proposed merger of Nynex Corp and Bell Atlantic if Nynex does not improve what he feels is a poor customer-service record in New York.
* Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc is planning to give away its experimental AIDS drug, Viracept, to those who have tried other protease-inhibitor treatments without success.
* Mobile Communications Holdings Inc has arranged $650 million in investor financing and plans to apply for a license from the Federal Communications Commission for a global satellite phone system.
* Sony named Vice Chairwoman Lucy Fisher to head its Columbia TriStar Pictures unit following the ouster of Chairman Mark Canton.
* Colony Capital acquired a 30-percent stake in a leading Asian luxury-hotel chain for $55 million, and said it would invest up to an additional $45 million.
* Kohlberg, Kravis, Roberts & Co is close to assembling a new buyout fund of $5 billion.
* Group Health and a unit of Kaiser are in merger talks.
* Columbia University sued Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp over use of the Columbia name.

* The National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) ordered Travelers Group Inc's Smith Barney unit and one of its brokers to pay $1 million in damages to a client who alleged the trader advised the purchase of stock that the trader was himself unloading.
* Philip Morris Cos Inc's Miller Brewing unit said it will cut the jobs of 500 employees, or 18.5 percent of its U.S. salaried work force.
* General Motors, looking to unearth rices buried under its lackluster stock, is signalling investors it wants to break up and shed much of its big GM Hughes Electronics unit. - Heard on the Street

* Bond investors bid farewell to the idea of an interest-rate increase by the Federal Reserve policymakers this month, sending Treasury prices soaring as much as 1-1/2 points Friday in their euphoria. - Credit Markets
